S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S076.name: Inability_Positive_Emotions
S076.description: Persistent inability to experience positive emotions (e.g., inability to experience happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings).

subtypes.Anhedonia for Happiness: Unable to feel happiness or joy even when good things happen.
subtypes.Lack of Satisfaction: Unable to experience satisfaction or pride even after achieving something good.
subtypes.Inability to Feel Love: Feeling numb to love or affection towards family or lovers.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where the mind feels empty and nothing is felt, as if all positive emotions are blocked.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.

subtypes.Scanning for Danger: Always scanning the surroundings and being alert to find potential threats or risks.
subtypes.Safety Checking: Repetitively confirming safety, such as checking exit locations or observing people around.
subtypes.Sustained Alertness: Unable to relax tension even in safe environments and maintaining a constant state of alertness.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.

subtypes.Auditory Startle: Startling excessively and flinching physically at sudden noises.
subtypes.Tactile Startle: Being extremely startled by unexpected physical contact.
subtypes.Visual Startle: Being greatly startled and wary of sudden appearances of people or rapid movements.
subtypes.Slow Recovery: Heart pounding and trembling for a long time after being startled, not calming down easily.

S082.name: Depersonalization_Derealization
S082.description: Altered sense of the reality of one's self or surroundings after a traumatic event.

subtypes.Depersonalization: Feeling detached from one's own body or mental processes, as if being an outside observer.
subtypes.Derealization: The surrounding environment feels unreal, dreamlike, distant, or distorted.
subtypes.Time Distortion: Time feels like it has stopped during the traumatic moment, or is perceived as moving extremely slowly or quickly.

patient_info.stressor: Jason had been reorganizing his small tax practice into a senior-consulting model when a long-time client arrived furious about an audit notice, cornered him in the office, and made a credible physical threat before police were called. In the first days afterward, Jason tried to keep working from home in Roanoke, but over two weeks he found himself unable to concentrate on returns, repeatedly unsure about decisions he normally made easily, and unable to recall a key part of the confrontation despite no injury or intoxication. His usual comforts—fishing plans, guitar, woodworking, and joking with his wife—felt flat, while he stayed tense around doorbells, office noises, and unexpected knocks. After missing several client deadlines and realizing he could not safely resume office hours, he contacted his primary care physician, who referred him for urgent psychiatric evaluation.

S082.name: Depersonalization_Derealization
S082.description: Altered sense of the reality of one's self or surroundings after a traumatic event.
S082.manifestation: What brings me in is that I keep having these moments where my own house or office feels unreal, like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: I sit down with a return I could normally handle in my sleep, and I end up rereading the same W-2s over and over, unable to decide simple things like whether to call a client or put the file aside.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).
S071.manifestation: I remember him crowding me in my office and I remember the police being there, but the middle part—what he said right before I reached for the phone—is just a blank no matter how hard I try to pull it up.

S076.name: Inability_Positive_Emotions
S076.description: Persistent inability to experience positive emotions (e.g., inability to experience happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings).
S076.manifestation: My wife tries to joke with me or asks about going fishing like we planned, and I know those things should feel good, but it's like the part of me that enjoys them has been switched off.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.
S079.manifestation: Even at home in Roanoke, I keep tracking every car door, every footstep on the porch, and where the exits are, like I need to be ready for someone to come at me again.

S080.name: Exaggerated_Startle_Response
S080.description: Exaggerated startle response to minor stimuli.
S080.manifestation: If the doorbell rings or my wife comes up behind me and touches my shoulder, I jump so hard my chest pounds and it takes several minutes before I can act normal again.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I've missed several client deadlines and stopped seeing people at the office because I don't trust myself to handle returns or keep the workplace safe right now.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about two weeks, ever since that client threatened me in my office.
